stem: Vivaan cooks rice on an LPG stove, then writes homework on paper made from wood pulp.

parts.text: Which claim best traces the resources and chooses a responsible reduction?

options.text: Cooking uses fuel gas and writing uses paper from trees; using a lid to cook faster and writing on both sides of the page reduces unnecessary use.
Stop cooking rice altogether because any cooking wastes fuel gas.
Writing on paper uses trees, but cooking rice on LPG uses no natural resource at all.
Clear, odourless LPG flame means no resource use or pollution, so no reduction is needed.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Everyday activities use natural resources directly or indirectly; identifying the fuel and the wood pulp, then reducing waste, is responsible use.

teacher.key_rationale: Cooking uses LPG (a fuel resource) and paper comes from trees; reducing waste without stopping necessary activities is responsible. Stopping cooking entirely, denying LPG as a resource, or treating a clear flame as zero impact all miss the hinge.
